## Constants

<a name="MaxSafeInt"></a>MaxSafeInt is 2^53 \- 1, the largest integer AsSafeInt accepts.

```go
const MaxSafeInt = 9007199254740991
```

## Variables

<a name="ErrDuplicateKey"></a>Errors returned by Parse and the As\* helpers. Callers match them with errors.Is.

```go
var (
    ErrDuplicateKey = errors.New("duplicate key")
    ErrTooLarge     = errors.New("input too large")
    ErrBOM          = errors.New("byte order mark not allowed")
    ErrInvalidUTF8  = errors.New("invalid utf-8")
    ErrTrailingData = errors.New("trailing data after json value")
    ErrType         = errors.New("unexpected type")
    ErrSyntax       = errors.New("invalid json syntax")
    ErrTooDeep      = errors.New("json nesting too deep")
)
```

## type [Member](<https://github.com/brii26/release-signer/blob/main/pkg/strictjson/strictjson.go#L65-L68>)

Member is one key/value pair of an object. Members keep their source order.

```go
type Member struct {
```

<a name="Value"></a>
## type [Value](<https://github.com/brii26/release-signer/blob/main/pkg/strictjson/strictjson.go#L71-L78>)

Value is a parsed JSON value. Only the field matching Kind is meaningful.

```go
type Value struct {
    Kind Kind
    Str  string
    Num  json.Number
    Bool bool
    Arr  []Value
    Obj  []Member
}
```

```go
func Parse(data []byte, maxSize int) (Value, error)
```

Parse urutan cek: size, BOM, UTF\-8, syntax \+ duplicate key, trailing data.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Duplicate keys are an error instead of silently keeping the last value.

```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/brii26/release-signer/pkg/strictjson"
)

func main() {
	_, err := strictjson.Parse([]byte(`{"a":1,"a":2}`), 1024)
	fmt.Println(errors.Is(err, strictjson.ErrDuplicateKey))
}
```

#### Output

```
true
```

</p>
</details>
